accepted.s: According to HDR 2025, India's position in the Human Development Index was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: 132nd among 191 countries, with an HDI value of 0.685
130th among 193 countries, with an HDI value of 0.685
134th among 193 countries, with an HDI value of 0.633
129th among 189 countries, with an HDI value of 0.676
accepted.x: HDR 2025 placed India at 130th among 193 countries, with an HDI value of 0.685 for 2023.
accepted.tq: Pair the report edition with both the rank and the number of countries.
accepted.sec: India's HDI rank by HDR edition

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's HDI trend:
1. India's HDI value increased from 0.514 in 2004 to 0.633 in 2021.
2. HDR 2025 revised India's 2022 HDI value to 0.676.
3. India's HDI value increased at approximately 1.42 per cent per year over three decades.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The recorded trend was from 0.514 in 2004 to 0.633 in 2021, with a long-term annual increase of about 1.42 per cent and a revised 2022 value of 0.676.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical trend separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: India's HDI rank by HDR edition

accepted.s: The title of the Human Development Report 2025 is
o: Beyond Income: Human Development in a Changing World
People, Prosperity and Planet in the Digital Age
A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI
Human Development and the Future of Work
accepted.x: The HDR 2025 is titled “A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI”.
accepted.tq: Use exact-title recall for a current report.
accepted.sec: India's HDI rank by HDR edition

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the HDR 2025 indicators mentioned for India?
o: Life expectancy 73 years, expected schooling 13 years and GNI per capita of $10,000
Life expectancy 72 years, expected schooling 15 years and GNI per capita of $7,500
Life expectancy 72 years, expected schooling 13 years and GNI per capita of $9,046.76
Life expectancy 70 years, expected schooling 13 years and GNI per capita of $9,046.76
accepted.x: For India, HDR 2025 records life expectancy of 72 years, expected years of schooling of 13 years and GNI per capita of $9,046.76.
accepted.tq: Match multiple figures belonging to the same report edition.
accepted.sec: India's HDI rank by HDR edition

accepted.s: Who conceived the Human Development Index in association with Amartya Sen?
accepted.x: The HDI was conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Amartya Sen; Inge Kaul was also part of the team.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the principal architect from other members of the team.
accepted.sec: HDI origin - economist, first HDR, publisher

accepted.s: The Human Development Report primarily compares countries with reference to
o: Environment, defence expenditure and literacy alone
accepted.x: The report compares countries on education, health and per-capita income as the principal dimensions of human development.
accepted.tq: Identify the three broad dimensions rather than a related development indicator.
accepted.sec: HDI origin - economist, first HDR, publisher

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Dimension)
a. Long and healthy life
b. Knowledge
c. Decent standard of living

List-II (Indicator)
i. GNI per capita in PPP dollars
ii. Life expectancy at birth
iii. Mean years and expected years of schooling
accepted.x: Long and healthy life is measured by life expectancy; knowledge by mean and expected years of schooling; and standard of living by GNI per capita in PPP dollars.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair linking life expectancy with a healthy life.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component indicator of the Human Development Index?
o: GNI per capita in PPP dollars
accepted.x: Environmental quality is not included in the HDI. The index uses life expectancy, schooling indicators and GNI per capita.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded environmental indicator among the three HDI dimensions.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the HDI:
1. It uses mean years of schooling for adults aged 25 years and above.
2. It uses expected years of schooling at school-entry age.
3. It uses GDP per capita rather than GNI per capita.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. HDI uses GNI per capita, not GDP per capita, for the income dimension.
accepted.tq: Use the GDP–GNI confusable-pair distinction.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: The HDI is calculated as the
o: Arithmetic mean of the three raw indicators
Geometric mean of the three normalised dimension indices
Median of the three country-level indices
Weighted sum of GDP, literacy and life expectancy
accepted.x: HDI is the geometric mean of the three normalised dimension indices: health, knowledge and standard of living.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the exact mathematical method from familiar alternatives.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: Why is the logarithm of income used in calculating the HDI?
o: To give greater importance to very high incomes
To exclude purchasing power differences between countries
To convert GNI into an environmental indicator
To reflect the diminishing importance of income at higher income levels
accepted.x: The logarithm of income reflects diminishing importance of additional income as income levels rise.
accepted.tq: Link the mathematical operation to its economic interpretation.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: The goalposts for life expectancy at birth used in HDI calculation are
accepted.x: The minimum and maximum goalposts for life expectancy at birth are 20 and 85 years.
accepted.tq: Recall paired minimum–maximum goalposts.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs of goalposts is correctly matched with the schooling indicator?
1. Mean years of schooling — 0 to 15 years
2. Expected years of schooling — 0 to 18 years
3. GNI per capita — $100 to $75,000
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct: mean schooling is normalised between 0 and 15 years, expected schooling between 0 and 18 years, and GNI per capita between $100 and $75,000.
accepted.tq: Verify each minimum–maximum pair before choosing the coded option.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: For cross-country comparison in the income dimension of HDI, income is expressed in
o: Domestic currency at the market exchange rate only
accepted.x: HDI uses GNI per capita in PPP dollars to permit fairer cross-country comparisons; the conversion is based on 2011 ICP surveys.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact adjustment used for international comparison.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT captured by the HDI, although it is related to human development?
accepted.x: HDI does not capture human security. It also does not directly capture inequality, poverty, empowerment, participation or the environment.
accepted.tq: Separate the core index indicators from wider human-development concerns.
accepted.sec: Components - what is in and what is not

accepted.s: India was placed at which position in HDR 2025 among the following countries listed in relation to India?
o: Above China and Sri Lanka but below Bhutan
Below China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan, but above Nepal
Below Nepal and Myanmar but above China
accepted.x: China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan ranked above India, while Nepal, Myanmar and Pakistan ranked below India.
accepted.tq: Arrange countries by their stated positions relative to the reference country.
accepted.sec: India vs neighbours and BRICS (HDR 2025)

accepted.s: Which one of the following countries ranked immediately at the same HDI level as India in HDR 2025?
accepted.x: Bangladesh and India were both shown at rank 130 in the HDR 2025 comparison.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an equal-ranked country from countries above and below India.
accepted.sec: India vs neighbours and BRICS (HDR 2025)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's position in HDR 2025:
1. Sri Lanka ranked higher than India.
2. Maldives ranked higher than India.
3. India was the lowest-ranked among the five original BRICS countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Sri Lanka and Maldives ranked above India, and Brazil, Russia, China and South Africa all ranked above India among the original BRICS members.
accepted.tq: Combine neighbour comparison with the BRICS comparison instead of treating them separately.
accepted.sec: India vs neighbours and BRICS (HDR 2025)

accepted.s: The two persistent weaknesses flagged for India in the HDR 2025 discussion were
o: Low life expectancy and low school enrolment
accepted.x: The report identified gender inequality and income inequality as India's two persistent weaknesses.
accepted.tq: Recall the report’s diagnostic issues rather than general economic problems.
accepted.sec: India vs neighbours and BRICS (HDR 2025)

accepted.s: Which country occupied the first position in HDR 2025?
accepted.x: Iceland ranked first in HDR 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the latest edition with its top-ranked country.
accepted.sec: Top-ranked countries by edition

accepted.s:
Match the following Human Development Report editions with the country ranked first.

a. HDR 2025
a. Iceland
b. HDR 2023-24
b. Switzerland
c. HDR 2021-22
c. Norway
accepted.x: Iceland ranked first in HDR 2025, while Switzerland ranked first in both HDR 2023-24 and HDR 2021-22.

accepted.s: Norway occupied the first position in which of the following Human Development Report editions?
accepted.x: Norway ranked first in HDR 2019.
accepted.tq: Match a historical edition with its top-ranked country.
accepted.sec: Top-ranked countries by edition

accepted.s: India's HDI value of 0.685 in HDR 2025 places it in which category?
accepted.x: An HDI value from 0.550 to 0.699 falls in the medium human development category. India's 0.685 is just below the high-category threshold of 0.700.
accepted.tq: Apply the category threshold to the given numerical value.
accepted.sec: HDI categories and India's place

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the HDI category thresholds?
o: Very high: 0.900 and above; High: 0.800–0.899; Medium: 0.600–0.799; Low: below 0.600
Very high: 0.750 and above; High: 0.650–0.749; Medium: 0.500–0.649; Low: below 0.500
Very high: 0.850 and above; High: 0.700–0.849; Medium: 0.500–0.699; Low: below 0.500
Very high: 0.800 and above; High: 0.700–0.799; Medium: 0.550–0.699; Low: below 0.550
accepted.x: The categories are very high at 0.800 and above, high at 0.700–0.799, medium at 0.550–0.699, and low below 0.550.
accepted.tq: Compare all four thresholds carefully, especially the boundary values.
accepted.sec: HDI categories and India's place

accepted.s: The ‘Kerala Model’ in the context of State human development refers to Kerala’s position as
o: The State with the highest income inequality alone
The State with the lowest HDI in India
The first State to publish a Human Development Report
A consistently top-performing State in human development
accepted.x: Kerala consistently tops Indian States in human development and is commonly associated with the Kerala Model.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a broad development model from the separate state-report milestone.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: Which group of States is identified as occupying the lowest end of the State human-development ranking?
o: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
West Bengal, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh are identified among the lowest-ranking States in human development.
accepted.tq: Recall the low-performing group rather than the consistently high-performing States.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: District-level HDI estimates prepared by NITI Aayog and State planning bodies are particularly useful because they
o: Replace the national HDI with GDP rankings
Show sharper intra-State differences in human development
accepted.x: District-level estimates reveal sharper intra-State gaps that may be concealed by State-level averages.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of disaggregated indicators to a regional-development scenario.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s:
With reference to rural and urban multidimensional poverty headcount ratios, which statement is correct?
1. Andhra Pradesh recorded 7.71 per cent in rural areas and 2.20 per cent in urban areas.
2. India recorded 19.28 per cent in rural areas and 5.27 per cent in urban areas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Both statements are correct. The cited figures show substantially higher rural than urban multidimensional poverty in both Andhra Pradesh and India.
accepted.tq: Compare the rural and urban rows before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the intensity and MPI score for Andhra Pradesh and India in the cited comparison?
o: AP: 41.12 per cent and 0.025; India: 44.39 per cent and 0.066
AP: 44.39 per cent and 0.066; India: 41.12 per cent and 0.025
AP: 41.12 per cent and 0.066; India: 44.39 per cent and 0.025
AP: 44.39 per cent and 0.025; India: 41.12 per cent and 0.066
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded intensity of 41.12 per cent and an MPI score of 0.025, while India's corresponding figures were 44.39 per cent and 0.066.
accepted.tq: Keep the intensity percentage and MPI value paired with the correct State or country.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s MPI score declined from 0.053 in 2015-16 to 0.025 in 2019-21. This represents approximately
accepted.x: The MPI score fell by approximately half, from 0.053 to 0.025, over the cited period.
accepted.tq: Estimate the percentage change from the two given values.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: Among the States, Andhra Pradesh ranked which position on the basis of the cited MPI comparison?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked ninth among States in the cited multidimensional poverty comparison.
accepted.tq: Recall the rank associated with the MPI dataset, not the HDI rank.
accepted.sec: State HDI - AP rank and state reports

accepted.s: Which district had the lowest multidimensional-poverty headcount ratio among the Andhra Pradesh districts listed?
accepted.x: West Godavari had the lowest listed headcount ratio at 2.42 per cent and an MPI of 0.010.
accepted.tq: Identify the minimum value before comparing the district options.

b. Guntur

 d. Chittoor

o: 9.20 per cent overall, 5.81 per cent rural and 10.96 per cent urban poverty
9.20 per cent overall, 10.96 per cent rural and 5.81 per cent urban poverty
21.92 per cent overall, 10.96 per cent rural and 9.20 per cent urban poverty
10.96 per cent overall, 9.20 per cent rural and 5.81 per cent urban poverty
